transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-20
Start time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood Solutions), Sofia Alvarez (CloudForge Head Partnerships), Evan Kim (CloudForge Platform Eng), Priya Nair (CloudForge Solutions), Daniel Brooks (CloudForge Marketplace PM)

Summary (auto): quick alignment on marketplace listing and a reference arch for Private/VPC integration, plus next steps and owners.

00:00:05 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining.. uh.. we'll run about 40 minutes. agenda is marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for a CloudForge-hosted private offering, and then next steps. does that sound right, Sofia?
00:00:22 Sofia Alvarez: yep that works. and Daniel from our marketplace team is here to cover the onboarding bits.
00:00:30 Daniel Brooks: hi all, thanks. quick note — our listing process has a few legal & security checkpoints, so we'll want the SOC2 docs and a simple manifest for the deployment artifact.
00:00:45 Raj Patel: got it. we can supply SOC2 summary and an architecture diagram. question for Daniel — do you prefer a single AMI/container bundle or a multi-artifact manifest?
00:00:58 Daniel Brooks: we accept both, but marketplace UX prefers a single bundle for quick installs; the manifest approach is fine for advanced listings.
00:01:12 Priya Nair: from a technical standpoint, the big thing for our platform team is how the VPC peering / private link works; we run strict egress rules. can you walk through the recommended network pattern?
00:01:27 Raj Patel: sure. high-level, Redwood Private can be deployed as a VPC-hosted instance behind your marketplace orchestrator; we recommend a three-tier pattern: control-plane in a management VPC with cross-account IAM roles, data plane in a customer VPC with interface endpoints, and optional transit gateway for multi-region. we'll share a diagram.
00:01:50 Evan Kim: interface endpoints.. are you using AWS PrivateLink or some other pattern? some of our customers are on GCP too.
00:01:58 Raj Patel: we support PrivateLink on AWS; for GCP it's VPC peering + Private Service Connect. there are slight naming mismatches in our docs, i'll make sure the diagram clarifies cloud-specific variants.
00:02:12 Liam O'Connor: (interject) also note our runtime uses short-lived keys for KV cache encryption; we can integrate with customer KMS or CloudForge KMS referrals depending on the deployment mode.
00:02:25 Sofia Alvarez: good — security will want KMS details and an ability to use their existing HSMs. can you provide an example with BYOK?
00:02:35 Raj Patel: yes, BYOK flows are supported; we'll include the KMS integration section with the manifest. there might be a small ops step to bootstrap keys for the first run.
00:02:48 Maya Chen: quick commercial Q — for marketplace listings we can support both pay-as-you-go hosted metering and reserved instances through CloudForge procurement; which route do you want to prioritize?
00:03:01 Daniel Brooks: we'd like to start with a marketplace listing that points to a private deploy option — many enterprise customers want to see they can bring their own VPC. pricing can be negotiable once we see pilot usage.
00:03:15 Priya Nair: on the pilot, we want a short checklist: install, provision KMS, test inference latency, run a small benchmark. can Redwood provide a benchmark script?
00:03:27 Raj Patel: yes, we have a lightweight benchmark harness (python script + sample prompts) we can share. we'll aim for 100-200 token prompt latency metrics and throughput numbers per instance type.
00:03:40 Evan Kim: logging and audit — do you emit structured audit logs for model requests and RBAC events? our security team needs retention settings.
00:03:50 Liam O'Connor: we emit structured logs and can push to a customer-managed S3 or GCS bucket, and we integrate with SIEMs via syslog/forwarder. retention is configurable and we'll document default retention and recommended settings for compliance.
00:04:05 Sofia Alvarez: SOC2 attestation — do you have a SOC2 report we can share internally?
00:04:11 Maya Chen: yes, we'll share the SOC2 Type II summary and an encrypted link to the full report via our security portal.
00:04:18 Daniel Brooks: great. for marketplace manifest we also need a short operations README. can you create a one-page install guide?
00:04:26 Raj Patel: yes, i'll put together a 1-pager + diagram.
00:04:32 Sofia Alvarez: timeline question: what's realistic to get a pilot listing live?
00:04:39 Maya Chen: if we move quickly on docs and the manifest, i think 3-4 weeks for a pilot is reasonable; depends on legal review time.
00:04:48 Daniel Brooks: legal typically wants 2 weeks for the contract review, security review may be another week — so your 3-4 weeks aligns.
00:04:58 Priya Nair: technical dependencies — do you require any privileged access into our infra to run the pilot?
00:05:05 Raj Patel: only temporary IAM role as per the manifest, or we can support a purely customer-managed install using bootstrap templates; we prefer role-based install for automated setup but will provide a manual alternative.
00:05:18 Evan Kim: are there any hard requirements for instance types? some customers want small GPUs, some want CPU-only.
00:05:26 Raj Patel: we support both; we'll publish recommended instance types by model/quantization profile. for bounded latency SLOs we recommend T4/RTX A-series or equivalent. CPU-only is possible for low-throughput workloads.
00:05:40 Maya Chen: let's talk artifacts to share today — Raj will share reference arch + 1-pager, SOC2 and benchmark harness. Daniel will share marketplace checklist and legal contact. Maya will set up demo week of March 10.
00:05:58 Liam O'Connor: small note on packaging: for marketplace we usually provide a Helm chart + container image; we can also support an AMI if CloudForge wants. Helm chart is easiest for customers that already run K8s.
00:06:12 Priya Nair: we'll likely prefer Helm; we run a managed k8s offering. please include values for node selectors and tolerations.
00:06:22 Raj Patel: sure, will include recommended Helm values for memory, GPU resources, and KV cache sizing.
00:06:30 Sofia Alvarez: about analytics and billing — do you emit usage records compatible with marketplace metering?
00:06:38 Maya Chen: yes, for hosted we emit per-token metering; for private marketplace listings we can emit usage records that your marketplace can ingest or we can provide sealed invoices if you prefer. we'll need to align on the metering format.
00:06:51 Daniel Brooks: we use a CSV-based metering ingest today, but can accept JSON. we'll send the spec.
00:06:59 Raj Patel: we'll map our metrics to both formats and include a small translator script if needed.
00:07:08 Priya Nair: any known limitations — e.g., models that don't support quantization or specific kernels?
00:07:15 Liam O'Connor: there are some open models that don't run well on older GPUs; we'll include a compatibility matrix and recommended quantization profiles. some kernels are cloud-vendor optimized and names might differ in docs (we sometimes call a kernel xformer-opt and others call it flash-attn), so apologies in advance for naming wobble.
00:07:34 Sofia Alvarez: ha yeah we've seen naming mismatches before, please keep the doc simple.
00:07:40 Maya Chen: ok to recap next steps — Raj to share reference arch, Helm values, 1-pager, benchmark harness by 2025-03-03; Daniel to share CF marketplace checklist + legal contact by 2025-02-27; Sofia to sync pricing and share proposals by 2025-03-05; Maya to schedule joint demo for week of 2025-03-10 and send invites by tomorrow.
00:08:05 Daniel Brooks: i'll also send the manifest template and a sample billing spec after the call.
00:08:12 Evan Kim: one small action — can you send test credentials for the benchmark environment?
00:08:17 Raj Patel: yes, we'll provide short-lived test creds and a sandbox project.
00:08:25 Priya Nair: thanks everyone, we'll review the docs once they're shared and pull in security for the SOC2.
00:08:32 Maya Chen: perfect. thanks all for the time. we'll follow up in writing with the action items and I'll send the invites.
00:08:40 [meeting ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional name misspells and acronyms may be inaccurate; speaker boundaries were inferred from Fireflies auto-transcript. Links referenced during call: marketplace checklist (link: drive.cloudforge.com/marketplace-checklist), draft manifest template (link: drive.redwood.com/rw-manifest-template), benchmark harness (link: github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness - private repo).
